slides:
LabLoop
- Robotic sample prep for contract research labs
- Seed round deck, 2026 (fictional test company)
- labloop.example.com

Problem
- Contract labs spend 30% of technician time on manual sample prep
- Errors in manual pipetting cause 1 in 20 assay re-runs

Traction
- 26 paying customers
- 40% month-on-month revenue growth since January
- $38k monthly recurring revenue

Market
- US contract-lab automation market: $4.1B TAM
- We target 2% market share by year 3

Competition
- No direct competitors
- Incumbent liquid handlers are 10x the price

Team
- CEO: 8 years at Thermo Fisher
- CTO: robotics PhD, ETH Zurich
- Team of 25 people

Financials and ask
- Revenue forecast: $5M in year 3
- Monthly burn: $90k
- Raising $3M seed at a $15M pre-money valuation

claims.quote: Raising $3M seed at a $15M pre-money valuation

check.reason: The valuation rests on the year-3 revenue forecast and current traction.
TAM x target share = $82M, so a $5M forecast is within the deck's own market maths.
Top-down figure with no source on the slide.

claims.quote: We target 2% market share by year 3

check.reason: A target, not evidence. It depends on there being no strong competitor.
Self-reported. 40% a month for 10 months would be about 29x growth, so MRR in January would have been about $1.3k.
The company's customers page archived 3 months ago lists 4 pilots, none paying. (Fixture example, not real data.)
Example only: funded companies sell robotic sample prep to contract labs.

sources.title: Fixture example
sources.quote: Example competitor sells automated sample prep to CROs

check.reason: A $90k monthly burn with 25 people is $3.6k per person per month, which is below US salary levels.
Self-reported. $38k / 26 customers = $1.5k per customer per month.

questions.text: Your deck says 26 paying customers, but your site listed 4 pilots three months ago. How many are paying today, and since when?
questions.why: Traction holds up the growth rate, the revenue forecast and the valuation.
questions.evidence_to_request: A customer list with contract start dates and the last 3 months of invoices

questions.text: Who else sells robotic sample prep to contract labs, and why do labs pick you?
questions.why: The 2% share target assumes no strong competitor.
questions.evidence_to_request: Win/loss notes from the last 10 deals

questions.text: How do 25 people fit in a $90k monthly burn?
questions.why: Either the team size or the burn rate is wrong, and the runway depends on which.
questions.evidence_to_request: Payroll summary and the last 6 months of bank statements
